title.zh: 卷二百〇五 列傳第九十二: 姦臣
title.raw: 卷二百〇五 列傳第九十二: 姦臣 Volume 205 Biographies 92: Treacherous Ministers

sentences.zh: 古之為史者，善惡備書，所以示勸懲也。

translations.literal: Of old, those who wrote history recorded both good and evil in full, in order to display encouragement and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times, historians recorded both virtue and vice in full, so that readers might be encouraged toward good and warned against evil.

sentences.zh: 故孔子修春秋，於亂臣賊子之事，無不具載，而楚之史名檮杌，皆以戒夫為惡者，使知所懼而不敢肆焉。

translations.literal: Therefore when Confucius compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals, he fully recorded all matters concerning rebellious ministers and unworthy sons, and Chu's history was named Taowu, all to warn those who commit evil, so that they would know what to fear and would not dare to act wantonly.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when Confucius edited the Spring and Autumn Annals, he left nothing out regarding rebellious ministers and traitorous sons; and Chu historians called their work the Taowu Annals—all alike meant to warn those who would do evil, so they would know fear and dare not run riot.

sentences.zh: 後世作史者，有酷吏、佞幸、姦臣、叛逆之傳，良有以也。

translations.literal: Historians of later ages have biographies of cruel officials, fawning favorites, treacherous ministers, and rebels—this is surely well-founded.
translations.idiomatic: Later historians included chapters on cruel officials, sycophantic favorites, treacherous ministers, and traitors—and they had good reason to do so.

sentences.zh: 元之舊史，往往詳於記善，略於懲惡，是蓋當時史臣有所忌諱，而不敢直書之爾。

translations.literal: The former histories of Yuan often record good in detail and treat punishment of evil briefly—this was surely because the historians of the time had taboos and did not dare write directly.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan's earlier annals often lavish detail on virtuous deeds while skimming over the punishment of vice—no doubt the court historians of that era felt certain topics were off limits and held their pens accordingly.

sentences.zh: 然姦巧之徒，挾其才術，以取富貴、竊威福，始則毒民誤國而終至於殞身亡家者，其行事之概，亦或散見於實錄編年之中，猶有春秋之意存焉。

translations.literal: Yet treacherous and cunning men, relying on their talents and arts to gain wealth and honor and usurp authority and blessings—beginning by poisoning the people and harming the state and finally reaching ruin of person and loss of family—the outline of their deeds may also be scattered through veritable records and chronological annals, still preserving something of the Spring and Autumn intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the outlines of scheming men who traded skill for wealth and power, who first poisoned the people and misled the state only to die ruined and leave their houses desolate—these can still be found scattered through the Veritable Records and chronological annals, preserving something of the Spring and Autumn spirit.

sentences.zh: 謹撮其尤彰著者，彙次而書之，作姦臣傳，以為世鑒。

translations.literal: I respectfully gather the most conspicuous, compile and arrange them in writing, making the Biography of Treacherous Ministers, as a mirror for the age.
translations.idiomatic: I have here gathered the most notorious cases, arranged them in order, and composed this chapter on treacherous ministers as a warning to the world.

sentences.zh: 而叛逆之臣，亦各以類附見云。

translations.literal: Rebels also are each attached by category in separate visibilities.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel ministers appear elsewhere in this work, grouped by kind.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬，回回人也。

translations.literal: Ahmad was a Muslim.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad was a Muslim.

sentences.zh: 不知其所由進，世祖中統三年，始命領中書左右部，兼諸路都轉運使，專以財賦之任委之。

translations.literal: It is not known by what path he advanced; in the third year of Zhongtong of Shizu, he was first ordered to head the Left and Right Departments of the Central Secretariat, concurrently serving as Commissioner of Transport for All Routes, entrusting him specially with fiscal duties.
translations.idiomatic: How he first rose to prominence is unknown. In the third year of the Zhongtong era, Kublai appointed him to head the left and right divisions of the Central Secretariat and also made him commissioner-general of transport for all circuits, entrusting him with fiscal authority alone.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬奏降條畫，宜諭各路運司。

translations.literal: Ahmad memorialized submitting regulations, which should be proclaimed to transport offices of each route.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad submitted a set of regulations for the transport commissioners in each circuit to follow.

sentences.zh: 明年，以河南鈞、徐等州俱有鐵冶，請給授宣牌，以興鼓鑄之利。

translations.literal: The next year, because Henan's Jun, Xu, and other prefectures all had iron smelteries, he requested granting authorization plaques to promote the profit of casting and forging.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, noting that Jun, Xu, and other prefectures in Henan all had ironworks, he requested authorization plaques to promote smelting and casting.

sentences.zh: 世祖陞開平府為上都，又以阿合馬同知開平府事，領左右部如故。

translations.literal: Shizu promoted Kaiping Prefecture to Shangdu, and again made Ahmad Associate Administrator of Kaiping Prefecture affairs, heading the Left and Right Departments as before.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai elevated Kaiping Prefecture to the status of Upper Capital and appointed Ahmad its associate administrator while leaving him in charge of the left and right secretariat divisions as before.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬奏以禮部尚書馬月合乃兼領已括戶三千，興煽鐵冶，歲輸鐵一百三萬七千斤，就鑄農器二十萬事，易粟輸官者凡四萬石。

translations.literal: Ahmad memorialized that Minister of Rites Ma Yuehenai should concurrently lead three thousand registered households, establish iron smelting, annually deliver 1,370,000 jin of iron, cast on the spot 200,000 agricultural implements, and exchange grain delivered to the government totaling 40,000 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad proposed that Minister of Rites Ma Yuehenai oversee three thousand registered households in iron smelting, delivering 1,370,000 jin of iron per year, casting 200,000 farm tools on site, and turning over 40,000 shi of grain to the government.

sentences.zh: 至元元年正月，阿合馬言：「太原民煮小鹽，越境販賣，民貪其價廉，競買食之，解鹽以故不售，歲入課銀止七千五百兩。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Zhiyuan, Ahmad said: "Taiyuan commoners boil small salt and sell it across borders; the people covet its low price and compete to buy and eat it, so Jie salt for this reason does not sell, and annual tax silver is only 7,500 taels.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first Zhiyuan year, Ahmad reported: "The people of Taiyuan boil small salt and sell it across district borders. Because it is cheap, everyone buys it, and the official salt from Jie Prefecture goes unsold. Annual salt-tax revenue amounts to only 7,500 taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 請自今歲增五千兩，無問僧道軍匠等戶，鈞出其賦，其民間通用小鹽從便。」

translations.literal: I request from this year to increase by 5,000 taels, regardless of monk, Daoist, military artisan households and the like, equally levying their tax; let common small salt used among the people be as convenient."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we add 5,000 taels to this year's quota, levying the tax equally from monks, Daoists, military households, artisans, and all others, while allowing the people to use small salt freely as they wish."

sentences.zh: 是年秋八月，罷領中書左右部，併入中書，超拜阿合馬為中書平章政事，進階榮祿大夫。

translations.literal: That autumn in the eighth month, the post of heading the Central Secretariat Left and Right Departments was abolished and merged into the Central Secretariat; Ahmad was promoted beyond regular appointment to Central Secretariat Grand Councillor, advanced in rank to Grand Master for Glorious Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, in the eighth month, the left and right secretariat divisions were abolished and merged into the Central Secretariat. Ahmad was promoted to grand councillor of the Central Secretariat and advanced to the rank of Grand Master for Glorious Happiness.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，立制國用使司，阿合馬又以平章政事兼領使職。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, the Bureau for Regulating National Expenditure was established; Ahmad again as Grand Councillor concurrently headed the commissioner post.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, the Bureau for Regulating National Expenditure was established, and Ahmad served as its commissioner while retaining his post as grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 久之，制國用使司奏：「以東京歲課布疏惡不堪用者，就以市羊於彼。

translations.literal: After some time, the Bureau memorialized: "Using Eastern Capital's annual tribute cloth that is coarse, poor, and unfit for use, exchange it there for purchasing sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later the bureau reported: "The annual tribute cloth from the Eastern Capital is coarse and unusable; it should be exchanged there for sheep.

sentences.zh: 真定、順天金銀不中程者，宜改鑄。

translations.literal: Zhending and Shuntian gold and silver not meeting standard should be recast.
translations.idiomatic: Gold and silver from Zhending and Shuntian that fail to meet standard should be recast.

sentences.zh: 別怯赤山出石絨，織為布火不能然，請遣官採取。」

translations.literal: Bieqiechi Mountain produces stone wool; woven into cloth fire cannot burn it—please send officials to collect it."
translations.idiomatic: Bieqiechi Mountain yields stone wool that, woven into cloth, will not burn in fire. Officials should be sent to collect it.

sentences.zh: 又言：「國家費用浩繁，今歲自車駕至都，已支鈔四千錠，恐來歲度支不足，宜量節經用。」

translations.literal: He also said: "State expenses are vast; this year from the imperial procession arriving at the capital, 4,000 ingots of paper money have already been disbursed—I fear next year's budget will be insufficient; expenditures should be measured and economized."
translations.idiomatic: It also reported: "State expenses are enormous. Since the imperial procession reached the capital this year, 4,000 ingots of paper money have already been spent. Next year's budget may fall short; expenditures should be trimmed."

sentences.zh: 十一月，制國用使司奏：「桓州峪所採銀礦，已十六萬斤，百斤可得銀三兩、錫二十五斤。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the Bureau memorialized: "Silver ore mined at Huanzhou Valley already amounts to 160,000 jin; per hundred jin one obtains three liang of silver and twenty-five jin of tin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the bureau reported: "Silver ore mined in Huanzhou Valley already totals 160,000 jin. From every hundred jin come three liang of silver and twenty-five jin of tin.

sentences.zh: 採礦所需，鬻錫以給之。」

translations.literal: What mining requires, sell tin to supply it."
translations.idiomatic: The tin needed for mining should be sold to cover costs.

sentences.zh: 悉從其請。

translations.literal: All were approved as requested.
translations.idiomatic: All these requests were approved.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，立尚書省，罷制國用使司，又以阿合馬平章尚書省事。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, the Imperial Secretariat was established and the Bureau for Regulating National Expenditure abolished; Ahmad again served as Grand Councillor of Imperial Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year, the Imperial Secretariat was established and the Bureau for Regulating National Expenditure abolished. Ahmad became grand councillor of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬為人多智巧言，以功利成效自負，衆咸稱其能。

translations.literal: Ahmad as a man was much given to clever speech; he took pride in practical benefit and effective results, and the multitude all praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad was clever and articulate, prided himself on delivering measurable results, and was widely regarded as capable.

sentences.zh: 世祖急於富國，試以行事，頗有成績。

translations.literal: Shizu was eager to enrich the state; testing him in action, there were considerable achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai, eager to enrich the state, tried him in office and found his performance creditable.

sentences.zh: 又見其與丞相線真、史天澤等爭辨，屢有以詘之，由是奇其才，授以政柄，言無不從，而不知其專愎益甚矣。

translations.literal: Also seeing him debate with Chancellor Xian Zhen, Shi Tianze, and others, repeatedly having arguments to refute them—thereby marveling at his talent, he granted him political power; his words were never not followed, yet not knowing his obstinacy grew ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai also watched him debate Chancellors Xian Zhen and Shi Tianze and repeatedly hold his own. Impressed by his talent, the emperor gave him real power; Ahmad's proposals were seldom refused—while his growing arrogance went unnoticed.

sentences.zh: 丞相安童含容久之，言於世祖曰：「臣近言尚書省、樞密院、御史臺，宜各循常制奏事，其大者從臣等議定奏聞，已有旨俞允。

translations.literal: Chancellor Antong had borne with him for a long time, and said to Shizu: "Your servant recently said the Imperial Secretariat, Bureau of Military Affairs, and Censorate should each follow regular procedure in memorializing; major matters should be deliberated by your servants and then memorialized—there is already an edict of approval.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Antong had long tolerated him, then told Kublai: "Your servant recently proposed that the Imperial Secretariat, Bureau of Military Affairs, and Censorate should each follow normal procedure in reporting affairs, with major matters deliberated by us before being submitted to Your Majesty. You were pleased to approve.

sentences.zh: 今尚書省一切以聞，似違前奏。」

translations.literal: Now the Imperial Secretariat reports everything directly, which seems to violate the previous memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Now the Imperial Secretariat reports everything directly to you, which seems to contradict that earlier decision.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「汝所言是。

translations.literal: Shizu said: "What you say is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said: "You are right.

sentences.zh: 豈阿合馬以朕頗信用，敢如是耶！

translations.literal: Could Ahmad, because I somewhat trust him, dare act thus!
translations.idiomatic: Has Ahmad grown so bold because I have trusted him?!

sentences.zh: 其不與卿議非是，宜如卿所言。」

translations.literal: That he does not deliberate with you is wrong; it should be as you say."
translations.idiomatic: He was wrong not to consult you. It shall be as you propose.

sentences.zh: 又言：「阿合馬所用部官，左丞許衡以為多非其人，然已得旨咨請宣付，如不與，恐異日有辭。

translations.literal: He also said: "Officials Ahmad employs—Left Chancellor Xu Heng considers many not the right men, yet they have already received edict for consultation and appointment; if not granted, I fear there will be excuse on another day.
translations.idiomatic: Antong added: "Many of the officials Ahmad has appointed are, in Left Chancellor Xu Heng's view, unfit for their posts. Yet they have already received imperial authorization. If we refuse them now, Ahmad may have grounds for complaint later.

sentences.zh: 宜試其能否，久當自見。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to test their ability; in time it will become clear of itself."
translations.idiomatic: Let us test their competence; time will tell.

sentences.zh: 世祖然之。

translations.literal: Shizu approved.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai agreed.

sentences.zh: 五月，尚書省奏括天下戶口，既而御史臺言，所在捕蝗，百姓勞擾，括戶事宜少緩。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Imperial Secretariat memorialized to register all households under Heaven; soon after the Censorate said that everywhere locusts were being caught, the people were troubled and harassed—the household registration matter should be somewhat delayed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Imperial Secretariat proposed a nationwide household registration. The Censorate then reported that locust-catching was exhausting the people everywhere and asked that the registration be postponed.

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The project was dropped.

sentences.zh: 初立尚書省時，有旨：「凡銓選各官，吏部擬定資品，呈尚書省，由尚書咨中書聞奏。」

translations.literal: When the Imperial Secretariat was first established, there was an edict: "For all selection and appointment of officials, the Ministry of Personnel determines rank and grade, presents to the Imperial Secretariat, and the Imperial Secretariat consults the Central Secretariat and memorializes."
translations.idiomatic: When the Imperial Secretariat was first established, an edict decreed: "For all official appointments, the Ministry of Personnel shall determine rank and grade and submit the list to the Imperial Secretariat, which shall consult the Central Secretariat before memorializing the throne.

sentences.zh: 至是，阿合馬擢用私人，不由部擬，不咨中書。

translations.literal: By this time, Ahmad promoted and employed private associates, not going through the ministry's nomination, not consulting the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: By now Ahmad was promoting his own men without ministry nomination or Central Secretariat consultation.

sentences.zh: 丞相安童以為言，世祖令問阿合馬。

translations.literal: Chancellor Antong spoke of it; Shizu ordered Ahmad questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Antong raised the issue, and Kublai ordered Ahmad questioned.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬言：「事無大小，皆委之臣，所用之人，臣宜自擇。」

translations.literal: Ahmad said: "Matters great and small are all entrusted to your servant; the people your servant employs, your servant should choose himself."
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad replied: "Great and small affairs alike are entrusted to me. I ought to choose my own subordinates.

sentences.zh: 安童因請：「自今唯重刑及遷上路緫管，始屬之臣，餘事並付阿合馬，庶事體明白。」

translations.literal: Antong thereupon requested: "From now only heavy punishments and transfers of route administrators should belong to your servant; all other matters be handed to Ahmad—then the body of affairs will be clear."
translations.idiomatic: Antong then proposed: "Henceforth only capital cases and appointments of route administrators should require our deliberation. Let all other matters go to Ahmad, so responsibilities are clear.

sentences.zh: 世祖俱從之。

translations.literal: Shizu approved both.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai approved both proposals.

sentences.zh: 八年三月，尚書省再以閱實戶口事，奏條畫詔諭天下。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighth year, the Imperial Secretariat again on verifying households memorialized regulations and an edict to proclaim throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the eighth year, the Imperial Secretariat again memorialized on verifying households and issued regulations by imperial edict throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 是歲，奏增太原鹽課，以千錠為常額，仍令本路兼領。

translations.literal: That year, it memorialized increasing Taiyuan salt tax, taking 1,000 ingots as the regular quota, still ordering this route to concurrently administer it.
translations.idiomatic: That year it proposed raising the Taiyuan salt tax to a fixed quota of 1,000 ingots, with the circuit continuing to administer collection.

sentences.zh: 九年，併尚書省入中書省，又以阿合馬為中書平章政事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the Imperial Secretariat was merged into the Central Secretariat, and Ahmad again became Central Secretariat Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Imperial Secretariat was merged into the Central Secretariat, and Ahmad was again made grand councillor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，又以其子忽辛為大都路緫管，兼大興府尹。

translations.literal: The next year, his son Khoshin was again made Metropolitan Route Administrator, concurrently Daxing Prefecture Magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: The following year his son Khoshin was appointed metropolitan route administrator and concurrently magistrate of Daxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 右丞相安童見阿合馬擅權日甚，欲救其弊，乃奏大都路緫管以次多不稱職，乞選人代之。

translations.literal: Right Chancellor Antong, seeing Ahmad's usurpation of power daily worsen, wished to remedy its harm, and memorialized that Metropolitan Route administrators and below were mostly unfit for office, requesting selection of men to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Right Chancellor Antong, seeing Ahmad's power grow daily more unchecked, sought to curb the abuse and memorialized that most metropolitan route officials were unfit, asking permission to replace them.

sentences.zh: 尋又奏：「阿合馬、張惠，挾宰相權，為商賈，以網羅天下大利，厚毒黎民，困無所訴。」

translations.literal: Soon he again memorialized: "Ahmad and Zhang Hui, wielding chancellor power, act as merchants, netting all great profits under Heaven, heavily poisoning the common people, distressed with nowhere to appeal."
translations.idiomatic: He soon added: "Ahmad and Zhang Hui abuse their authority as chancellors to trade as merchants, monopolizing the empire's greatest profits and grinding the people down with nowhere to turn for justice.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬曰：「誰為此言，臣等當與廷辯。」

translations.literal: Ahmad said: "Who spoke these words? Your servants should debate it at court."
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad demanded: "Who said this? We demand a debate before the court.

sentences.zh: 安童進曰：「省左司都事周祥，中木取利，罪狀明白。」

translations.literal: Antong advanced and said: "Provincial Left Department Director Zhou Xiang, taking profit from timber in transit—the criminal facts are clear."
translations.idiomatic: Antong replied: "Zhou Xiang, director of the left department in the secretariat, profited from timber contracts. The evidence is clear.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「若此者，徵畢當顯黜之。」

translations.literal: Shizu said: "For such as this, when the investigation is complete he should be openly dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said: "When the investigation is finished, such men must be publicly dismissed.

sentences.zh: 既而樞密院奏以忽辛同僉樞密院事，世祖不允曰：「彼賈胡，事猶不知，況可責以機務耶！」

translations.literal: Soon after the Bureau of Military Affairs memorialized making Khoshin Associate Administrator of the Bureau; Shizu did not approve, saying: "That merchant—he does not even know affairs; how can he be charged with critical duties!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Bureau of Military Affairs proposed making Khoshin its associate administrator, Kublai refused: "That merchant-boy scarcely understands affairs. How can he be entrusted with state secrets?!"

sentences.zh: 十二年，伯顏帥師伐宋，既渡江，捷報日至。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Bayan led troops to attack Song; having crossed the Yangtze, victory reports arrived daily.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Bayan led the army against the Song. After crossing the Yangtze, reports of victory arrived daily.

sentences.zh: 世祖命阿合馬與姚樞、徒單公履、張文謙、陳漢歸、楊誠等，議行鹽、鈔法于江南，及貿易藥材事。

translations.literal: Shizu ordered Ahmad together with Yao Shu, Tushan Gonglu, Zhang Wenqian, Chen Hangu, Yang Cheng, and others to deliberate implementing salt and paper-money laws in Jiangnan, and matters of trading medicinal materials.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai ordered Ahmad, Yao Shu, Tushan Gonglu, Zhang Wenqian, Chen Hangu, Yang Cheng, and others to deliberate on introducing salt and paper-currency regulations in the south and on trade in medicinal goods.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬奏：「樞云：『江南交會不行，必致小民失所。』

translations.literal: Ahmad memorialized: "Shu said: 'Jiangnan exchange notes will not circulate—this will surely cause common people to lose their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad reported: "Yao Shu said: 'If the southern exchange notes are not honored, the common people will lose their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 公履云：『伯顏已嘗榜諭交會不換，今亟行之，失信於民。』

translations.literal: Gonglu said: 'Bayan has already posted proclamations that exchange notes will not be exchanged; to hurry implementation now would break faith with the people.'
translations.idiomatic: Tushan Gonglu said: 'Bayan has already posted notices promising the notes would not be forcibly exchanged. To act now would break faith with the people.'

sentences.zh: 文謙謂『可行與否，當詢伯顏』。

translations.literal: Wenqian said 'whether it can be done should be asked of Bayan.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenqian said the matter should be referred to Bayan.

sentences.zh: 漢歸及誠皆言：『以中統鈔易其交會，何難之有。』」

translations.literal: Hangu and Cheng both said: 'Using Zhongtong notes to exchange their exchange notes—what difficulty is there?'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hangu and Yang Cheng both said: 'Exchanging them for Zhongtong notes—what difficulty is there?'

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「樞與公履，不識事機。

translations.literal: Shizu said: "Shu and Gonglu do not understand the opportune moment.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said: "Shu and Gonglu do not understand the moment.

sentences.zh: 朕嘗以此問陳巖，巖亦以宋交會速宜更換。

translations.literal: I once asked Chen Yan about this; Yan also held that Song exchange notes should quickly be replaced.
translations.idiomatic: I once asked Chen Yan, and he too said the Song notes should be replaced at once.

sentences.zh: 今議已定，當依汝言行之。」

translations.literal: Now deliberation is settled; it should follow your words and be implemented."
translations.idiomatic: The matter is settled. Do as you propose.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「北鹽藥材，樞與公履皆言可使百姓從便販鬻。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Regarding northern salt and medicinal materials, Shu and Gonglu both said the common people could be allowed to sell conveniently as they wish.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad also reported: "On northern salt and medicinal goods, Shu and Gonglu both favored letting the people trade freely.

sentences.zh: 臣等以為此事若小民為之，恐紊亂不一。

translations.literal: Your servants consider that if common people do this matter, I fear disorder and lack of uniformity.
translations.idiomatic: We believe that if commoners handled this trade, the market would fall into chaos.

sentences.zh: 擬於南京、衛輝等路，籍括藥材，蔡州發鹽十二萬斤，禁諸人私相貿易。」

translations.literal: We propose at Nanjing, Weihui, and other routes to register and seize medicinal materials; Cai Prefecture to issue 120,000 jin of salt, forbidding all persons private mutual trade."
translations.idiomatic: We propose registering medicinal stocks in Nanjing, Weihui, and other circuits, issuing 120,000 jin of salt from Cai Prefecture, and forbidding private trade.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「善，其行之。」

translations.literal: Shizu said: "Good—implement it."
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said: "Good. Carry it out."

sentences.zh: 十二年，阿合馬又言：「比因軍興之後，減免編民征稅，又罷轉運司官，令各路緫管府兼領課程，以致國用不足。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Ahmad again said: "Recently because after military campaigns tax levies on registered commoners were reduced, and transport commissioner offices were abolished, ordering each route's chief administrator's office to concurrently administer tax items—this caused state revenue to be insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Ahmad reported: "After the recent campaigns, taxes on registered households were cut and transport commissioners abolished, with circuit chief administrators taking over revenue collection. State income has fallen short.

sentences.zh: 臣以為莫若驗戶數多寡，遠以就近，立都轉運司，量增舊額，選廉幹官分理其事。

translations.literal: Your servant considers it best to verify household numbers more or less, distant assigned to near, establish metropolitan transport commissioners, measure and increase old quotas, select honest and capable officials to divide and manage the matter.
translations.idiomatic: I propose re-establishing metropolitan transport offices based on household counts, assigning distant districts to nearby ones, raising the old quotas, and appointing honest, capable officials to manage collection.

sentences.zh: 應公私鐵鼓鑄，官為局賣，仍禁諸人毋私造銅器。

translations.literal: All public and private iron casting and forging should be sold through government bureaus; still forbid all persons from privately making copper vessels.
translations.idiomatic: All iron casting, public and private, should be sold through government agencies, and private manufacture of copper vessels should be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 如此，則民力不屈，而國用充矣。」

translations.literal: Thus the people's strength will not be bent, and state revenue will be full."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the people will not be crushed, and state revenue will be ample.

sentences.zh: 乃奏立諸路轉運司，以亦必烈金、札馬剌丁、張暠、富珪、蔡德潤、紇石烈亨、阿里和者、完顏迪、姜毅、阿老瓦丁、倒剌沙等為使。

translations.literal: Thereupon it memorialized establishing transport commissioners for each route, appointing Yibilie Jin, Jamal al-Din, Zhang Gao, Fu Gui, Cai Derun, Hesilie Heng, Ali Hezhe, Wanyan Di, Jiang Yi, Alaoding, Daolasha, and others as commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioners were then established for each circuit, with Yibilie Jin, Jamal al-Din, Zhang Gao, Fu Gui, Cai Derun, Hesilie Heng, Ali Hezhe, Wanyan Di, Jiang Yi, Alaoding, Daolasha, and others appointed.

sentences.zh: 有亦馬都丁者，以負官銀得罪而罷，既死，而所負尚多，中書省奏議裁處。

translations.literal: There was one Yimaduding who, for owing official silver, was guilty and dismissed; having died, what he owed was still much—the Central Secretariat memorialized deliberating disposition.
translations.idiomatic: One Yimaduding had been dismissed for owing official silver to the government. He died still heavily in debt, and the Central Secretariat memorialized on how to settle the account.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「此財穀事，其與阿合馬議之。」

translations.literal: Shizu said: "This is a fiscal matter—deliberate it with Ahmad."
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said: "This is a fiscal matter. Take it up with Ahmad."

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，世祖以西京饑，發粟萬石賑之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year, Shizu because Western Capital suffered famine issued 10,000 shi of grain for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year, famine struck the Western Capital, and Kublai released 10,000 shi of grain for relief.

sentences.zh: 又諭阿合馬宜廣貯積，以備闕乏。

translations.literal: He also instructed Ahmad to broadly store reserves to prepare for shortage.
translations.idiomatic: He also told Ahmad to build up grain reserves against future shortages.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬奏：「自今御史臺非白省，毋擅召倉庫吏，亦毋究索錢穀數。

translations.literal: Ahmad memorialized: "From now the Censorate, unless it informs the Secretariat, must not on its own summon granary clerks, nor investigate and demand money and grain accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad memorialized: "Henceforth the Censorate must not summon granary clerks or audit revenue accounts without first notifying the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及集議中書不至者，罪之。」

translations.literal: And those who do not attend when the Central Secretariat convenes deliberation—punish them."
translations.idiomatic: Censors who fail to attend secretariat deliberations should be punished.

sentences.zh: 其沮抑臺察如此。

translations.literal: Thus he obstructed and suppressed censorial investigation.
translations.idiomatic: In this way he hobbled the censorate's oversight.

sentences.zh: 四月，中書左丞崔斌奏曰：「先以江南官冗，委任非人，遂命阿里等澄汰之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Central Secretariat Left Chancellor Cui Bin memorialized: "Previously because Jiangnan offices were redundant and appointments were unfit persons, an order was given for Ali and others to clarify and eliminate them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, Left Chancellor Cui Bin memorialized: "Because offices in the south were overstaffed with unfit appointees, Ali and others were ordered to weed them out.

sentences.zh: 今已顯有徵驗，蔽不以聞，是為罔上。

translations.literal: Now clear evidence has appeared, yet it was concealed and not reported—this is deceiving the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Clear evidence has now emerged, yet it was concealed from the throne—this is deceiving Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 杭州地大，委寄非輕，阿合馬溺於私愛，乃以不肖子抹速忽充達魯花赤，佩虎符，此豈量才授任之道。」

translations.literal: Hangzhou's territory is large; the trust entrusted is not light—Ahmad, drowning in private affection, nevertheless used his unworthy son Masuhu as darughachi, wearing the tiger tally—how is this the way of measuring talent and granting office?"
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou is a weighty post. Yet Ahmad, blinded by favoritism, installed his worthless son Masuhu as darughachi with the tiger tally. This is hardly the way to measure talent and grant office.

sentences.zh: 又言：「阿合馬先自陳乞免其子弟之任，乃今身為平章，而子若姪或為行省參政，或為禮部尚書、將作院達魯花赤、領會同館，一門悉處要津，自背前言，有虧公道。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Ahmad first himself memorialized requesting exemption of his sons and younger relatives from office—yet now he himself is Grand Councillor, while sons and nephews are either route-province Associate Administrators, or Ministers of Rites, or darughachi of the Directorate of Palace Construction, or heads of the Hall of United Submission—one household all placed at critical passes, betraying his earlier words, harming public fairness."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Ahmad once asked that his sons and nephews be excused from office. Yet now, as grand councillor himself, he has placed them throughout the government—sons and nephews as provincial administrators, Minister of Rites, darughachi of the Directorate of Palace Construction, head of the Hall of United Submission. The whole family holds the choke points of power, in plain violation of his earlier pledge and of public fairness.

sentences.zh: 有旨並罷黜之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered them all dismissed.

sentences.zh: 然終不以是為阿合馬罪。

translations.literal: Yet in the end this was not taken as Ahmad's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ahmad himself was never held accountable.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘗謂淮西宣慰使昂吉兒曰：「夫宰相者，明天道，察地理，盡人事，兼此三者，乃為稱職。

translations.literal: Shizu once said to Huaixi Pacification Commissioner Angier: "A chancellor illuminates Heaven's Way, discerns Earth's patterns, exhausts human affairs—combining these three, only then is he fit for office.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai once told Huaixi Pacification Commissioner Angier: "A true chancellor comprehends Heaven's way, discerns Earth's patterns, and exhausts human affairs. Only one who unites all three is fit for the post.

sentences.zh: 阿里海牙、麥朮丁等，亦未可為相，回回人中，阿合馬才任宰相。」

translations.literal: Alaihaiya, Maijueding, and others also cannot serve as chancellor; among Muslims, only Ahmad's talent can bear the chancellorship."
translations.idiomatic: Neither Alaihaiya nor Maijueding is fit to be chancellor. Among the Muslims, only Ahmad has the talent for it.

sentences.zh: 其為上所稱道如此。

translations.literal: Thus he was praised and commended by the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which the emperor held him.

sentences.zh: 十六年四月，中書奏立江西榷茶運司，及諸路轉運鹽使司、宣課提舉司。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixteenth year, the Central Secretariat memorialized establishing Jiangxi Tea Monopoly Transport Office, and transport salt commissioners for each route, and tax-item promotion offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the sixteenth year the Central Secretariat proposed establishing a Jiangxi tea monopoly transport office, circuit salt transport commissioners, and tax promotion offices.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以忽辛為中書右丞。

translations.literal: Before long, Khoshin was made Central Secretariat Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Khoshin was appointed right chancellor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，中書省奏：「阿塔海、阿里言，今立宣課提舉司，官吏至五百餘員。

translations.literal: The next year, the Central Secretariat memorialized: "Atahai and Ali say that now establishing tax promotion offices, officials reach more than five hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Central Secretariat reported: "Atahai and Ali say the new tax promotion offices employ more than five hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 左丞陳嚴、范文虎等言其擾民，且侵盜官錢。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Chen Yan, Fan Wenhui, and others say they harass the people and moreover embezzle official money.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Chen Yan, Fan Wenhui, and others say they harass the people and embezzle public funds.

sentences.zh: 乞罷之。」

translations.literal: They request abolishing them."
translations.idiomatic: They ask that the offices be abolished.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬奏：「昨有言旨籍江南糧數，屢移文取索，不以實上。

translations.literal: Ahmad memorialized: "Yesterday there was an oral edict to register Jiangnan grain numbers; repeated documents were sent to demand them, yet they were not reported truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad replied: "There was recently an oral edict to register grain figures for the south. Repeated demands were sent, but truthful returns were never made.

sentences.zh: 遂與樞密院、御史臺及廷臣諸老集議，謂設立運司，官多俸重，宜諸路立提舉司，都省、行省各委一人任其事。

translations.literal: Thereupon together with the Bureau of Military Affairs, Censorate, and elder court ministers we convened deliberation, saying establishing transport offices meant many officials and heavy salaries—it was fitting for each route to establish promotion offices, with the Metropolitan Secretariat and Branch Secretariat each appointing one person to handle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs, the Censorate, and senior ministers then met and agreed that full transport offices meant too many officials on heavy salaries. Each circuit should have a promotion office, with one appointee each from the metropolitan and branch secretariats.

sentences.zh: 今行省未嘗委人，即請罷之，乃歸咎臣等。

translations.literal: Now the Branch Secretariat never appointed anyone, yet immediately requests abolition—this turns blame on your servants.
translations.idiomatic: The branch secretariat never appointed anyone, yet they now ask to abolish the offices and blame us.

sentences.zh: 然臣所委人，有至者僅兩月，計其侵用凡千一百錠，以彼所管四年較之，又當幾何？

translations.literal: Yet among those your servant appointed, some served only two months; calculating their embezzlement totals 1,100 ingots—compared with what they administered over four years, how much more would it be?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the men I appointed served as little as two months and embezzled 1,100 ingots. What would the total be over the four years the others have held office?

sentences.zh: 今立提舉司，未及三月而罷，豈非恐彼姦弊呈露，故先自言以絕跡耶？

translations.literal: Now the promotion offices were established less than three months before abolition—is this not fearing their wicked abuses would be exposed, so speaking first themselves to cut off traces?
translations.idiomatic: The promotion offices have existed less than three months, and already they seek abolition. Are they not afraid their own corruption will be exposed, and so speak first to cover their tracks?

sentences.zh: 宜令御史臺遣能臣同往，凡有非法，具以實聞。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to order the Censorate to send capable ministers together to go; wherever there is illegality, fully report truthfully.」
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate should send capable officials to investigate jointly and report every irregularity in full.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「阿合馬所言是，其令臺中選人以往。

translations.literal: Kublai said: 「What Ahmad has said is correct; order the Censorate to select men to go.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said, "What Ahmad has said is correct. Order the Censorate to select officials to go.

sentences.zh: 若己能自白，方可責人。」

translations.literal: Only if one can clear oneself may one hold others accountable.」
translations.idiomatic: Only when one can clear oneself may one hold others accountable."

sentences.zh: 阿合馬嘗奏宜立大宗正府。

translations.literal: Ahmad once memorialized that the Great Office of the Clan should be established.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad once memorialized that a Great Office of the Clan should be established.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「此事豈卿輩所宜言，乃朕事也。

translations.literal: Kublai said: 「How is this matter for people like you to speak of? It is my affair.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said, "How is this a matter for people like you to speak of? It is my affair.

sentences.zh: 然宗正之名，朕未之知，汝言良是，其思之。」

translations.literal: Yet as for the name Grand Regulator of the Clan, I do not know it; what you say is quite right—think it over.」
translations.idiomatic: Yet as for the title Grand Regulator of the Clan, I do not know it. What you say is quite right—consider it further."

sentences.zh: 阿合馬欲理筭江淮行省平章阿里伯、右丞燕帖木兒立行省以來一切錢穀，奏遣不魯合荅兒、劉思愈等往檢覈之，得其擅易命官八百員，自分左右司官，及鑄造銅印等事，以聞。

translations.literal: Ahmad wished to audit all revenue and grain since Ali Bo, Branch Secretariat Commissioner of the Jiang-Huai Branch Secretariat, and Yan Temür, Right Vice Commissioner, had established the Branch Secretariat; he memorialized to dispatch Buluqadar, Liu Siyu, and others to inspect and verify, finding that they had on their own authority replaced eight hundred appointed officials, divided left and right bureau officials themselves, and cast copper seals, among other matters, and reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad sought to audit all revenue and grain accounts since Ali Bo, Branch Secretariat Commissioner of the Jiang-Huai Branch Secretariat, and Yan Temür, Right Vice Commissioner, had established that secretariat. He memorialized that Buluqadar, Liu Siyu, and others be sent to investigate, and they found that the two men had on their own authority replaced eight hundred appointed officials, divided left and right bureau officials among themselves, and cast copper seals, among other offenses, which they reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「阿里伯等何以為辭？」

translations.literal: Kublai said: 「What excuses do Ali Bo and the others have?」
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said, "What excuses do Ali Bo and the others offer?"

sentences.zh: 阿合馬曰：「彼謂行省昔嘗鑄印矣。

translations.literal: Ahmad said: 「They say the Branch Secretariat once cast seals in the past.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad said, "They claim the Branch Secretariat once cast seals in the past.

sentences.zh: 臣謂昔以江南未定，故便宜行之，今與昔時事異。

translations.literal: Your subject says that formerly, because Jiangnan was not yet settled, they therefore acted as expedient; now matters differ from those times.
translations.idiomatic: I say that in the past, because Jiangnan was not yet pacified, such expedient measures were justified, but present circumstances differ from those times.

sentences.zh: 又擅支糧四十七萬石，奏罷宣課提舉司及中書遣官理筭，徵鈔萬二千錠有奇。」

translations.literal: Moreover, they arbitrarily disbursed forty-seven thousand shi of grain; memorialized to abolish the Office of Salt Tax Commissions and dispatched Central Secretariat officials to audit, collecting a little over twelve thousand ingots of paper currency.」
translations.idiomatic: They also arbitrarily disbursed forty-seven thousand shi of grain. Ahmad memorialized to abolish the Office of Salt Tax Commissions and dispatched Central Secretariat officials to conduct an audit, recovering a little over twelve thousand ingots of paper currency."

sentences.zh: 二人竟以是就戮。

translations.literal: The two men were in the end executed on these grounds.
translations.idiomatic: On these grounds, the two men were ultimately executed.

sentences.zh: 時阿合馬在位日久，益肆貪橫，援引奸黨郝禎、耿仁，驟升同列，陰謀交通，專事蒙蔽，逋賦不蠲，衆庶流移，京兆等路歲辦課至五萬四千錠，猶以為未實。

translations.literal: At this time Ahmad had long been in office and grew ever more greedy and overbearing; he brought in wicked associates Hao Zhen and Geng Ren, rapidly promoting them to equal rank, secretly conspiring and colluding, devoting himself to deception, not remitting overdue taxes, and the common people drifting away in displacement; the Jingzhao Circuit and others annually supplied revenue reaching fifty-four thousand ingots, yet he still considered this insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: By then Ahmad had held power for many years and grew ever greedier and more overbearing. He brought in wicked associates Hao Zhen and Geng Ren, rapidly promoting them to equal rank, and secretly conspired with them to deceive the court. Overdue taxes went unremitted, and the common people were driven from their homes. The Jingzhao Circuit and other circuits annually supplied fifty-four thousand ingots in revenue, yet he still regarded the amount as insufficient.

sentences.zh: 民有附郭美田，輒取為己有。

translations.literal: Where the people had fine fields near the city walls, he would seize them for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the people possessed fine fields near the city walls, he would seize them for himself.

sentences.zh: 內通貨賄，外示威刑，廷中相視，無敢論列。

translations.literal: Within he accepted bribes; without he displayed punitive authority; in court they looked at one another, none daring to speak out.
translations.idiomatic: Within the court he accepted bribes; without he displayed punitive authority. Officials looked at one another in silence, and none dared to speak against him.

sentences.zh: 有宿衛士秦長卿者，慨然上書發其姦，竟為阿合馬所害，斃于獄。

translations.literal: There was a palace guard named Qin Changqing who, indignant, submitted a memorial exposing his wickedness, and in the end was harmed by Ahmad and died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: A palace guard named Qin Changqing, indignant at Ahmad's conduct, submitted a memorial exposing his crimes, but was ultimately killed by Ahmad and died in prison.

sentences.zh: 事見長卿傳。

translations.literal: The matter is recorded in Changqing's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The affair is recorded in Changqing's biography.

sentences.zh: 十九年三月，世祖在上都，皇太子從。

translations.literal: In the third month of the nineteenth year, Kublai was at Shangdu, and the Crown Prince accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the nineteenth year, Kublai was at Shangdu, accompanied by the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 有益都千戶王著者，素志疾惡，因人心憤怨，密鑄大銅鎚，自誓願擊阿合馬首。

translations.literal: There was a Yidu chiliarch named Wang Zhu who had long harbored hatred of evil; because popular resentment was inflamed, he secretly cast a great copper mace and vowed to himself that he wished to strike Ahmad's head.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Yidu chiliarch named Wang Zhu who had long detested wickedness. Moved by the people's anger, he secretly cast a great copper mace and vowed to strike Ahmad down.

sentences.zh: 會妖僧高和尚，以祕術行軍中，無驗而歸，詐稱死，殺其徒，以尸欺衆，逃去，人亦莫知。

translations.literal: It happened that the sorcerer-monk Gao Heshang, practicing secret arts in the army, returned without effect, falsely claimed death, killed his disciples, deceived the multitude with a corpse, and fled; no one knew where he had gone.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that a sorcerer-monk named Gao Heshang, who had practiced secret arts in the army, returned without success. He feigned death, killed his disciples, and deceived the crowd with a corpse before fleeing; no one knew where he had gone.

sentences.zh: 著乃與合謀，以戊寅日，詐稱皇太子還都作佛事，結八十餘人，夜入京城。

translations.literal: Wang Zhu then joined him in plotting; on the day wuyin, falsely claiming the Crown Prince was returning to the capital to perform Buddhist rites, he gathered more than eighty men and entered the capital by night.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhu then joined him in a plot. On the day wuyin, they falsely claimed the Crown Prince was returning to the capital to perform Buddhist rites, gathered more than eighty men, and entered the capital by night.

sentences.zh: 旦遣二僧詣中書省，令市齋物，省中疑而訊之，不伏。

translations.literal: At dawn he sent two monks to the Central Secretariat to order vegetarian provisions purchased; the Secretariat grew suspicious and interrogated them, but they did not confess.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he sent two monks to the Central Secretariat to purchase vegetarian provisions for the rites. The Secretariat grew suspicious and questioned them, but they did not confess.

sentences.zh: 及午，著又遣崔緫管矯傳令旨，俾樞密副使張易發兵若干，以是夜會東宮前。

translations.literal: By midday Wang Zhu again sent Supervisor Cui to forge and transmit an imperial order, directing Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Zhang Yi to dispatch a certain number of troops to assemble before the Eastern Palace that night.
translations.idiomatic: By midday Wang Zhu sent Supervisor Cui to forge and transmit an imperial order directing Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Zhang Yi to dispatch troops to assemble before the Eastern Palace that night.

sentences.zh: 易莫察其偽，即令指揮使顏義領兵俱往。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi did not detect the forgery and immediately ordered Commandant Yan Yi to lead the troops there together.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi did not detect the forgery and immediately ordered Commandant Yan Yi to lead the troops there.

sentences.zh: 著自馳見阿合馬，詭言太子將至，令省官悉候于宮前。

translations.literal: Wang Zhu himself galloped to see Ahmad, falsely saying the Crown Prince was about to arrive, and ordered all Secretariat officials to wait before the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhu himself rode in haste to see Ahmad, falsely reporting that the Crown Prince was about to arrive, and ordered all Secretariat officials to wait before the palace.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬遣右司郎中脫歡察兒等數騎出關，北行十餘里，遇其衆，偽太子者責以無禮，盡殺之，奪其馬，南入健德門。

translations.literal: Ahmad dispatched Right Bureau Director Tuo Huancha'er and several horsemen out of the gate; traveling north more than ten li, they met the band; the false Crown Prince rebuked them for discourtesy, killed them all, seized their horses, and entered the Jiande Gate from the south.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad dispatched Right Bureau Director Tuo Huancha'er and several horsemen out of the gate. After traveling north more than ten li, they met the band. The false Crown Prince rebuked them for discourtesy, killed them all, seized their horses, and entered the capital through the Jiande Gate from the south.

sentences.zh: 夜二鼓，莫敢何問，至東宮前，其徒皆下馬，獨偽太子者立馬指揮，呼省官至前，責阿合馬數語，著即牽去，以所袖銅鎚碎其腦，立斃。

translations.literal: At the second watch of the night, none dared question them; arriving before the Eastern Palace, his followers all dismounted; only the false Crown Prince remained mounted directing affairs, summoned the Secretariat officials forward, rebuked Ahmad in several words; Wang Zhu immediately pulled him away and with the copper mace hidden in his sleeve shattered his skull, killing him on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: At the second watch of the night, no one dared challenge them. When they reached the Eastern Palace, the conspirators all dismounted while the false Crown Prince alone remained mounted and directed affairs. He summoned the Secretariat officials forward and rebuked Ahmad in a few words. Wang Zhu immediately pulled Ahmad aside and, with the copper mace hidden in his sleeve, shattered his skull, killing him instantly.

sentences.zh: 繼呼左丞郝禎至，殺之。

translations.literal: He then summoned Left Vice Commissioner Hao Zhen and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Left Vice Commissioner Hao Zhen and killed him.

sentences.zh: 囚右丞張惠。

translations.literal: He imprisoned Right Vice Commissioner Zhang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He imprisoned Right Vice Commissioner Zhang Hui.

sentences.zh: 樞密院、御史臺、留守司官皆遙望，莫測其故。

translations.literal: Officials of the Bureau of Military Affairs, the Censorate, and the Office of the Capital Guardian all watched from afar, unable to fathom the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the Bureau of Military Affairs, the Censorate, and the Office of the Capital Guardian watched from afar, unable to fathom what was happening.

sentences.zh: 尚書張九思自宮中大呼，以為詐，留守司達魯花赤博敦，遂持梃前，擊立馬者墜地，弓矢亂發，衆奔潰，多就禽。

translations.literal: Secretary Zhang Jiusi shouted loudly from within the palace that it was a fraud; the Office of the Capital Guardian's darughachi Bodun then advanced with a club, struck the mounted man to the ground, bows and arrows were loosed in disorder, the crowd fled in rout, and many were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Zhang Jiusi shouted from within the palace that it was a fraud. The Office of the Capital Guardian's darughachi Bodun then advanced with a club and struck the mounted man to the ground. Bows and arrows were loosed in confusion, the conspirators fled in rout, and many were captured.

sentences.zh: 高和尚等逃去，著挺身請囚。

translations.literal: Gao Heshang and others fled; Wang Zhu stepped forward and asked to be imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Heshang and the others fled, while Wang Zhu stepped forward and offered himself for arrest.

sentences.zh: 中丞也先帖木兒馳奏世祖，時方駐蹕察罕腦兒，聞之震怒，即日至上都。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Yesun Temür galloped to report to Kublai; at the time he was just encamped at Chaghan Na'ur; hearing this he was greatly enraged and reached Shangdu that same day.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Yesun Temür rode in haste to report to Kublai, who was then encamped at Chaghan Na'ur. Enraged upon hearing the news, Kublai reached Shangdu that same day.

sentences.zh: 命樞密副使孛羅、司徒和禮霍孫、參政阿里等馳驛至大都，討為亂者。

translations.literal: He ordered Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Boluo, Minister of Education Horchi, and Administration Commissioner Ali and others to ride post-haste to Dadu to suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Boluo, Minister of Education Horchi, Administration Commissioner Ali, and others to ride post-haste to Dadu to suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，獲高和尚于高梁河。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, Gao Heshang was captured at Gaoliang River.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengchen, Gao Heshang was captured at Gaoliang River.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，孛羅等至都。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, Boluo and the others reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinsi, Boluo and the others reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 壬午，誅王著、高和尚于市，皆醢之，并殺張易。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, Wang Zhu and Gao Heshang were executed in the marketplace; both were minced; Zhang Yi was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renwu, Wang Zhu and Gao Heshang were executed in the marketplace and their bodies minced. Zhang Yi was also put to death.

sentences.zh: 著臨刑大呼曰：「王著為天下除害，今死矣，異日必有為我書其事者。」

translations.literal: Facing execution Wang Zhu shouted loudly: 「Wang Zhu has removed a scourge for the realm; now I die; someday there will surely be one who writes this affair for me.」
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution, Wang Zhu shouted, "Wang Zhu has removed a scourge for the realm. Now I die, but someday someone will surely record what I have done."

sentences.zh: 阿合馬死，世祖猶不深知其姦，令中書毋問其妻子。

translations.literal: When Ahmad died, Kublai still did not fully know his wickedness and ordered the Central Secretariat not to investigate his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: After Ahmad's death, Kublai still did not fully understand his crimes and ordered the Central Secretariat not to investigate his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 及詢孛羅，乃盡得其罪惡，始大怒曰：「王著殺之，誠是也。」

translations.literal: When he questioned Boluo, he then fully learned his crimes and wickedness, and only then said in great anger: 「Wang Zhu killed him—truly that was right.」
translations.idiomatic: When he questioned Boluo, he learned the full extent of Ahmad's crimes and only then said in great anger, "Wang Zhu killed him—and rightly so."

sentences.zh: 乃命發墓剖棺，戮尸于通玄門外，縱犬啗其肉。

translations.literal: He then ordered the tomb opened and the coffin disinterred, the corpse exposed outside the Tongxuan Gate, and dogs set loose to devour his flesh.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Ahmad's tomb opened and coffin disinterred, the corpse exposed outside the Tongxuan Gate, and dogs set loose to devour the flesh.

sentences.zh: 百官士庶，聚觀稱快。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners gathered to watch and expressed satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners gathered to watch and rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 子姪皆伏誅，沒入其家屬財產。

translations.literal: Sons and nephews all submitted to execution; his household dependents and property were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: His sons and nephews were all executed, and the property of his household was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 其妾有名引住者，籍其藏，得二熟人皮於櫃中，兩耳具存，一閹豎專掌其扃鐍，訊問莫知為何人，但云「詛時，置神座其上，應驗甚速」。

translations.literal: His concubine, one named Yinzhu, had her stores registered; two human skins of acquaintances were found in a cabinet, both ears intact; one eunuch attendant exclusively managed its lock and bolt; under interrogation none knew whose they were, but he only said, 「When cursing and imprecating, one placed a spirit seat upon them, and the response was very swift.」
translations.idiomatic: His concubine, a woman named Yinzhu, had her stores inventoried, and two human skins of acquaintances were found in a cabinet, both ears intact. A eunuch attendant exclusively managed the lock and bolt. Under interrogation no one knew whose skins they were, but the attendant said only, "When casting curses, one placed a spirit seat upon them, and the results came very swiftly."

sentences.zh: 又以絹二幅，畫甲騎數重，圍守一幄殿，兵皆張弦挺刃內向，如擊刺之為者。

translations.literal: Moreover, on two bolts of silk were painted several ranks of armored horsemen surrounding and guarding a curtained hall; the soldiers all had bows drawn and blades extended inward, as if in the act of striking and stabbing.
translations.idiomatic: There were also two bolts of silk on which were painted several ranks of armored horsemen surrounding a curtained hall, all with bows drawn and blades extended inward, as though in the act of striking and stabbing.

sentences.zh: 畫者陳其姓。

translations.literal: The painter gave his surname as Chen.
translations.idiomatic: The painter gave his surname as Chen.

sentences.zh: 又有曹震圭者，嘗推筭阿合馬所生年月。

translations.literal: There was also one Cao Zhengwei who had once calculated the year and month of Ahmad's birth.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a man named Cao Zhengwei who had once calculated the year and month of Ahmad's birth.

sentences.zh: 王臺判者，妄引圖讖。

translations.literal: Wang Taipan had recklessly cited prognostic charts and omens.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Taipan had recklessly cited prognostic charts and omens.

sentences.zh: 皆言涉不軌。

translations.literal: All were said to involve sedition.
translations.idiomatic: All were said to involve sedition.

sentences.zh: 事聞，敕剝四人者皮以徇。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict ordered the flaying of the four men's skins as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported, an edict ordered the four men flayed as a public warning.

sentences.zh: 盧世榮，大名人也。

translations.literal: Lu Shirong was a man of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shirong was a native of Daming.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬專政，世榮以賄進，為江西榷茶運使，後以罪廢。

translations.literal: When Ahmad monopolized government, Lu Shirong advanced through bribery and became Jiangxi Tea Monopoly Transport Commissioner; later he was dismissed for a crime.
translations.idiomatic: While Ahmad monopolized power, Lu Shirong advanced through bribery and was appointed Jiangxi Tea Monopoly Transport Commissioner, but was later dismissed for a crime.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬死，朝廷之臣諱言財利事，皆無以副世祖裕國足民之意。

translations.literal: When Ahmad died, the court ministers avoided speaking of fiscal matters and none could fulfill Kublai's intent to enrich the state and provide for the people.
translations.idiomatic: After Ahmad's death, court ministers avoided speaking of fiscal matters, and none could fulfill Kublai's intent to enrich the state and provide for the people.

sentences.zh: 有桑哥者，薦世榮有才術，謂能救鈔法，增課額，上可裕國，下不損民。

translations.literal: There was one named Sangge who recommended Lu Shirong as talented and skilled, saying he could rescue the paper currency system, increase revenue quotas, enrich the state above, and not harm the people below.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Sangge recommended Lu Shirong as talented and skilled, saying he could rescue the paper currency system, increase revenue quotas, enrich the state, and do so without harming the people.

sentences.zh: 世祖召見，奏對稱旨。

translations.literal: Kublai summoned him for an audience; his memorial responses accorded with the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai summoned him for an audience, and his responses pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 至元二十一年十一月辛丑，召中書省官與世榮廷辨，論所當為之事，右丞相和禮霍孫等守正不撓，為強詞所勝，與右丞麥朮丁，參政張雄飛、溫迪罕皆罷，復起安童為右丞相，以世榮為右丞，而左丞史樞，參政不魯迷失海牙、撒的迷失，參議中書省事拜降，皆世榮所薦也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the twenty-first year of Zhiyuan, on the day xinchou, he summoned Central Secretariat officials to debate Lu Shirong in court on matters that ought to be done; Right Chancellor Horchi and others held to rectitude without yielding but were overcome by forceful argument; together with Right Vice Commissioner Mai Zhuding and Administration Commissioners Zhang Xiongfei and Undihan they were all dismissed; An Tong was again raised as Right Chancellor, and Lu Shirong was made Right Vice Commissioner; while Left Vice Commissioner Shi Shu, Administration Commissioners Buluomishi Haiya and Sadiemishi, and Secretariat Deliberator Baixiang were all recommended by Lu Shirong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the twenty-first year of Zhiyuan, on the day xinchou, Kublai summoned Central Secretariat officials to debate Lu Shirong in court over proposed reforms. Right Chancellor Horchi and others held firmly to principle but were overcome by Lu Shirong's forceful arguments. Horchi, Right Vice Commissioner Mai Zhuding, and Administration Commissioners Zhang Xiongfei and Undihan were all dismissed. An Tong was restored as Right Chancellor, and Lu Shirong was appointed Right Vice Commissioner. Left Vice Commissioner Shi Shu, Administration Commissioners Buluomishi Haiya and Sadiemishi, and Secretariat Deliberator Baixiang were all Lu Shirong's nominees.

sentences.zh: 世榮既驟被顯用，即日奉旨中書整治鈔法，遍行中外，官吏奉法不虔者，加以罪。

translations.literal: Lu Shirong, having suddenly been prominently employed, that same day received an edict for the Central Secretariat to rectify the paper currency system, promulgating it throughout the realm; officials and clerks who did not reverently observe the law were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shirong, having suddenly risen to prominence, that same day received an edict directing the Central Secretariat to rectify the paper currency system and promulgate the reforms throughout the realm. Officials who failed to observe the law faithfully were punished.

sentences.zh: 翌日，同右丞相安童奏：「竊見老幼疾病之民，衣食不給，行乞於市，非盛世所宜見。

translations.literal: The next day, together with Right Chancellor An Tong he memorialized: 「Your subject has observed that aged, young, and sick people lack food and clothing and beg in the markets—this is not what a flourishing age ought to witness.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, together with Right Chancellor An Tong, he memorialized, "I have observed that the aged, the young, and the sick lack food and clothing and beg in the markets. Such a sight is unworthy of a flourishing age.

sentences.zh: 宜官給衣糧，委各路正官提舉其事。」

translations.literal: It is fitting that the state supply clothing and grain, entrusting the chief officials of each circuit to oversee the matter.」
translations.idiomatic: The state should supply them with clothing and grain, and the chief officials of each circuit should be charged with overseeing the matter."

sentences.zh: 又奏懷孟竹園、江湖魚課，及襄淮屯田事。

translations.literal: He also memorialized on the bamboo groves of Huai-Meng, the fish levies of the rivers and lakes, and the garrison farms of Xiang-Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized on the bamboo groves of Huai-Meng, the fish levies on rivers and lakes, and the garrison farms of Xiang-Huai.

sentences.zh: 越三日，安童奏：「世榮所陳數事，乞詔示天下。」

translations.literal: Three days later An Tong memorialized: 「The several matters Lu Shirong has presented—your subject asks that they be proclaimed to the realm by edict.」
translations.idiomatic: Three days later An Tong memorialized, "The several reforms Lu Shirong has proposed should be proclaimed to the realm by edict."

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「除給丐者衣食外，並依所陳。」

translations.literal: Kublai said: 「Except for supplying clothing and food to beggars, all shall follow what has been presented.」
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said, "Except for supplying clothing and food to beggars, approve all that has been proposed."

sentences.zh: 乃下詔云：「金銀係民間通行之物，自立平準庫，禁百姓私相買賣，今後聽民間從便交易。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued saying: 「Gold and silver are goods in common circulation among the people; since the establishment of the Equalization Offices, private buying and selling by the common people has been forbidden; hereafter the people are permitted to trade as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued: "Gold and silver are goods in common circulation among the people. Since the establishment of the Equalization Offices, private trade by commoners has been forbidden. Hereafter the people may trade freely as they see fit.

sentences.zh: 懷孟諸路竹貨，係百姓栽植，有司拘禁發賣，使民重困，又致南北竹貨不通；

translations.literal: Bamboo goods in the Huai-Meng circuits were planted by the common people; the authorities restricted and compelled their sale, causing the people heavy distress and also causing north-south bamboo goods not to circulate;
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo goods in the Huai-Meng circuits are planted by commoners. Authorities have restricted and compelled their sale, causing the people great hardship and preventing north-south trade in bamboo;

sentences.zh: 今罷各處竹監，從民貨賣收稅。

translations.literal: now the bamboo offices in each place are abolished, and the people are permitted to sell goods and pay tax.
translations.idiomatic: the bamboo offices in each region are now abolished, and the people may sell their goods and pay tax.

sentences.zh: 江湖魚課，已有定例，長流採捕，貧民恃以為生，所在拘禁，今後聽民採用。

translations.literal: Fish levies on rivers and lakes already have fixed regulations; long stretches are harvested and fished, and the poor rely on this for livelihood; everywhere they have been restricted; hereafter the people are permitted to harvest and use them.
translations.idiomatic: Fish levies on rivers and lakes already have fixed regulations. The poor rely on fishing for their livelihood, yet everywhere they have been restricted. Hereafter the people may fish freely.

sentences.zh: 軍國事務往來，全資站驛，馬價近增，又令各戶供使臣飲食，以致疲弊，今後除驛馬外，其餘官為支給。」

translations.literal: Military and state affairs in transit rely entirely on courier stations and post relays; horse prices have recently risen, and moreover each household has been made to supply envoys with food and drink, causing exhaustion and ruin; hereafter, apart from relay horses, the rest shall be supplied by the state.」
translations.idiomatic: Military and state affairs in transit rely entirely on courier stations and post relays. Horse prices have recently risen, and households have also been required to supply envoys with food and drink, causing widespread exhaustion. Hereafter, apart from relay horses, the state shall provide all other supplies."

sentences.zh: 既而中書省又奏：「鹽每引十五兩，國家未嘗多取，欲便民食。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the Central Secretariat again memorialized: 「Salt is fifteen taels per yin; the state has never taken much, wishing to convenience the people's food.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the Central Secretariat memorialized again, "Salt is taxed at fifteen taels per yin. The state has never taken much, wishing to make salt affordable for the people.

sentences.zh: 今官豪詭名罔利，停貨待價，至一引賣八十貫，京師亦百二十貫，貧者多不得食。

translations.literal: Now officials and powerful families use false names to seek profit, hoard goods awaiting prices, until one yin sells for eighty strings; in the capital also one hundred twenty strings; the poor mostly cannot obtain food.
translations.idiomatic: Now officials and powerful families hoard salt under false names to profit from inflated prices, until one yin sells for eighty strings, and in the capital for one hundred twenty strings. The poor can scarcely afford to eat.

sentences.zh: 議以二百萬引給商，一百萬引散諸路，立常平鹽局，或販者增價，官平其直以售，庶民用給，而國計亦得。」

translations.literal: It is proposed to supply two million yin to merchants, distribute one million yin to the various circuits, establish Ever-Normal Salt Offices, and when sellers raise prices, the state shall equalize the price for sale, so that the common people have supply and the state accounts also gain.」
translations.idiomatic: It is proposed to supply two million yin to merchants, distribute one million yin to the various circuits, and establish Ever-Normal Salt Offices. When sellers raise prices, the state shall sell at a stabilized price so that the people are supplied and the state revenue is secured."

sentences.zh: 世祖從之。

translations.literal: Kublai assented.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 世榮居中書未十日，御史中丞崔彧言其不可為相，大忤旨，下彧吏按問，罷職。

translations.literal: Lu Shirong had been in the Central Secretariat less than ten days when Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu said he was unfit to serve as chancellor, greatly offending the imperial intent; Cui Yu was handed to officials for investigation and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shirong had been in the Central Secretariat less than ten days when Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu declared him unfit to serve as chancellor, greatly offending the emperor. Cui Yu was handed over for investigation and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 世榮言：「京師富豪戶釀酒酤賣，價高味薄，且課不時輸，宜一切禁罷，官自酤賣。」

translations.literal: Lu Shirong said: 「Wealthy households in the capital brew wine and sell it; the price is high and the taste thin, and moreover the tax is not paid on time; it is fitting to forbid this entirely and have the state sell wine itself.」
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shirong said, "Wealthy households in the capital brew and sell wine at high prices and poor quality, and fail to pay taxes on time. All private wine sales should be forbidden, and the state should sell wine itself."

sentences.zh: 明年正月壬午，世祖御香殿，世榮奏：「臣言天下歲課鈔九十三萬二千六百錠之外，臣更經畫，不取於民，裁抑權勢所侵，可增三百萬錠。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, on the day renwu, Kublai held court in the Hall of Incense; Lu Shirong memorialized: 「Your subject says that beyond the realm's annual revenue of nine hundred thirty-two thousand six hundred ingots of paper currency, through further planning, without taking from the people, by curbing what the powerful have encroached upon, three million ingots can be added.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year, on the day renwu, Kublai held court in the Hall of Incense. Lu Shirong memorialized, "Beyond the realm's annual revenue of nine hundred thirty-two thousand six hundred ingots of paper currency, I can, through further planning and without taxing the people, curb the encroachments of the powerful and add three million ingots.

sentences.zh: 初未行下，而中外已非議，臣請與臺院面議上前行之。」

translations.literal: At first it had not yet been promulgated, yet within and without there was already criticism; your subject asks to discuss it face to face with the Censorate and Bureau before Your Majesty and then implement it.」
translations.idiomatic: The plan has not yet been promulgated, yet criticism has already arisen within and without the court. I ask to discuss it face to face with the Censorate and Bureau before Your Majesty and then implement it."

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「不必如此，卿但言之。」

translations.literal: Kublai said: 「There is no need for this; you need only speak.」
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said, "There is no need for that. Simply speak."

sentences.zh: 世榮奏：「古有榷酤之法，今宜立四品提舉司，以領天下之課，歲可得鈔千四百四十錠。

translations.literal: Lu Shirong memorialized: 「Antiquity had the method of monopolizing wine sales; now it is fitting to establish a Fourth-Rank Commissariat to oversee the realm's levies, annually obtaining one thousand four hundred forty ingots of paper currency.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shirong memorialized, "Antiquity had the method of monopolizing wine sales. A Fourth-Rank Commissariat should now be established to oversee the realm's levies, yielding one thousand four hundred forty ingots of paper currency annually.

sentences.zh: 自王文統誅後，鈔法虛弊，為今之計，莫若依漢、唐故事，括銅鑄至元錢，及製綾券，與鈔參行。」

translations.literal: Since Wang Wentong's execution, the paper currency system has been hollow and debased; for the present plan, nothing is better than following the precedents of Han and Tang, gathering copper to cast Zhiyuan coins, and making silk certificates to circulate jointly with paper currency.」
translations.idiomatic: Since Wang Wentong's execution, the paper currency system has grown hollow and debased. For the present, nothing is better than following Han and Tang precedents: gather copper to cast Zhiyuan coins and issue silk certificates to circulate alongside paper currency."

sentences.zh: 因以所織綾券上之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he presented the woven silk certificates he had made.
translations.idiomatic: He then presented the woven silk certificates he had prepared.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「便益之事，當速行之。」

translations.literal: Kublai said: 「Matters of benefit should be swiftly carried out.」
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said, "Beneficial reforms should be carried out swiftly."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「於泉、杭二州立市舶都轉運司，造船給本，令人商販，官有其利七，商有其三。

translations.literal: He again memorialized: 「At Quan and Hang two circuits establish Maritime Trade Chief Transport Offices, build ships and supply capital, send men to trade, the state having seven parts of the profit and merchants three.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again, "Establish Maritime Trade Chief Transport Offices at Quanzhou and Hangzhou, build ships and supply capital, and send men to trade. The state shall receive seven parts of the profit and the merchants three.

sentences.zh: 禁私泛海者，拘其先所蓄寶貨，官買之；

translations.literal: Those who privately sail the seas are forbidden; their previously accumulated treasures and goods are seized and purchased by the state;
translations.idiomatic: Private voyages at sea are forbidden. Previously accumulated treasures and goods shall be seized and purchased by the state;

sentences.zh: 匿者，許告，沒其財，半給告者。

translations.literal: those who conceal are permitted to be reported; their wealth is confiscated, half given to the informer.
translations.idiomatic: those who conceal goods may be reported; their wealth shall be confiscated, with half given to the informer.

sentences.zh: 今國家雖有常平倉，實無所畜。

translations.literal: Now although the state has Ever-Normal Granaries, in fact nothing is stored.
translations.idiomatic: Although the state maintains Ever-Normal Granaries, in fact nothing is stored in them.

sentences.zh: 臣將不費一錢，但盡禁權勢所擅產鐵之所，官立鑪鼓鑄為器鬻之，以所得利合常平鹽課，糴粟積於倉，待貴時糶之，必能使物價恒賤，而獲厚利。

translations.literal: Your subject will not spend a single coin, but will entirely forbid iron-producing places monopolized by the powerful, have the state establish furnaces to cast vessels and sell them, combine the profit obtained with Ever-Normal salt revenue, purchase grain and store it in granaries, and when prices are high sell it forth—this will surely keep commodity prices constantly low and obtain thick profit.
translations.idiomatic: I will spend not a single coin, but will forbid iron-producing sites monopolized by the powerful, establish state furnaces to cast and sell vessels, combine the profits with Ever-Normal salt revenue, purchase grain for storage, and sell when prices rise. This will surely keep commodity prices low and yield substantial profit.

sentences.zh: 國家雖立平準，然無曉規運者，以致鈔法虛弊，諸物踊貴。

translations.literal: Although the state has established equalization, yet there is none who understands regulation and transport, causing the paper currency system to be hollow and debased and all goods to soar in price.
translations.idiomatic: Although the state has established equalization offices, there is no one who understands regulation and transport, causing the paper currency system to grow debased and all goods to soar in price.

sentences.zh: 宜令各路立平準周急庫，輕其月息。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order each circuit to establish Equalization Emergency Relief treasuries and lighten the monthly interest.
translations.idiomatic: Each circuit should establish Equalization Emergency Relief treasuries with reduced monthly interest.

sentences.zh: 以貸貧民，如此，則貸者衆，而本且不失。

translations.literal: To lend to the poor—thus, borrowers will be many, yet the principal will not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: They should lend to the poor. Thus borrowers will be many, yet the principal will not be lost.

sentences.zh: 又，隨朝官吏增俸，州郡未及，可於各都立市易司，領諸牙儈人，計商人物貨，四十分取一，以十為率，四給牙儈，六為官吏俸。

translations.literal: Moreover, as court officials' salaries are increased, the prefectures and commanderies have not yet reached this; in each capital one may establish Market Exchange Offices, overseeing all brokers, assessing merchants' goods, taking one part in forty; using ten as the rate, four given to brokers and six as officials' salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as court officials' salaries are increased, prefectures and commanderies have not yet caught up. Market Exchange Offices may be established in each capital to oversee brokers, assess merchants' goods, and levy one part in forty. Of every ten parts collected, four go to brokers and six to officials' salaries.

sentences.zh: 國家以兵得天下，不藉糧餽，惟資羊馬，宜於上都、隆興等路，以官錢買幣帛易羊馬於北方，選蒙古人牧之，收其皮毛筋角酥酪等物，十分為率，官取其八，二與牧者。

translations.literal: The state gained the realm by arms, not relying on grain transport, but only on sheep and horses; it is fitting at Shangdu, Longxing, and other circuits to use state funds to buy silks and cloths and exchange for sheep and horses in the north, select Mongols to herd them, collect their hides, fur, sinew, horn, butter, and cheese and the like; using ten as the rate, the state takes eight and two go to the herders.
translations.idiomatic: The state gained the realm by arms and relies not on grain transport but on sheep and horses. At Shangdu, Longxing, and other circuits, state funds should be used to buy silks and cloths and exchange for sheep and horses in the north. Mongols should be selected to herd them and collect hides, fur, sinew, horn, butter, and cheese. Of every ten parts, the state takes eight and the herders receive two.

sentences.zh: 馬以備軍興，羊以充賜予。」

translations.literal: Horses to prepare for military campaigns; sheep to supply bestowals.」
translations.idiomatic: Horses are to supply military campaigns; sheep are to supply imperial bestowals."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「汝先言數事皆善，固當速行。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 「The several matters you spoke of earlier are all good and should indeed be swiftly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The several reforms you proposed earlier are all good and should indeed be carried out swiftly.

sentences.zh: 此事亦善，祖宗時亦欲行之而不果，朕當思之。」

translations.literal: This matter is also good; in the time of our forefathers they also wished to carry it out but did not succeed; I shall consider it.」
translations.idiomatic: This proposal is also good. Our forefathers wished to carry it out but did not succeed. I shall consider it."

sentences.zh: 世榮因奏曰：「臣之行事，多為人所怨，後必有譖臣者，臣實懼焉，請先言之。」

translations.literal: Lu Shirong thereupon memorialized saying: 「In carrying out affairs, your subject is much resented by others; afterward there will surely be those who slander your subject; your subject is truly afraid; I ask to speak of this first.」
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shirong then memorialized, "In carrying out my duties I provoke much resentment. There will surely be those who slander me afterward, and I am truly afraid. I ask to speak of this first."

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「汝言皆是，惟欲人無言者，安有是理。

translations.literal: Kublai said: 「What you say is all correct; only wishing that people have nothing to say—how could there be such a principle?
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said, "What you say is all correct. But to wish that people have nothing to say—how could there be such a thing?

sentences.zh: 汝無防朕，飲食起居間可自為防。

translations.literal: You need not guard against me; in eating, drinking, and daily life you may guard yourself.
translations.idiomatic: You need not guard against me. In eating, drinking, and daily life, guard yourself.

sentences.zh: 疾足之犬，狐不愛焉，主人豈不愛之。

translations.literal: A swift-footed hound—the fox does not love it; how could the master not love it?
translations.idiomatic: A swift-footed hound is hated by foxes, but how could its master fail to love it?

sentences.zh: 汝之所行，朕自愛也，彼姦偽者則不愛耳。

translations.literal: What you do, I myself love; only those wicked and false ones do not love it.
translations.idiomatic: What you do, I myself approve. Only the wicked and deceitful do not love it.
